notes: n_runs = 3, not 5 (the run only contains run_index 0-2 for eval-49|D); A1/A2/A6/G7a/G7b copied verbatim from the mechanical json (all pass, all 3 runs). Sub-sampling applied per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 carries null for those (not scored, not a pass). | G5 fail (runs 0,1): offered alias `you-key-square` = c3r4 on truthBoard `decision` carries the major-threat role 'a single square completing your four-in-a-row line' (zoneAnnotations.mjs:145 fallback branch), board-false there — c3r4 is a 2-of-4 minor cell on the decision board (visualize_board.sh 334553333255262 shows (*) at col3 row4 and lists only 'col5 row3 (O)' as a major). The sibling alias `you-major` (c5r3) gets the same text and IS true, which is why the defect is specific to reusing the completing-square role for the opponentPunishment cell. It is in requiredSet, so every run is obliged to wrap it. | G1 fail (run 2): 'finishes your four-in-a-row line so that you win on the spot' contradicts the rendered artifact the model saw — the link text says the better move 'completes your 7-shaped double threat in column 5', the afterBest Tactics list says 'immediate at c5r2 (you)', and the offered term glossary defines immediate_threat as 'a square where four-in-a-row completes on the very next move'. The assembled prompt even carries the explicit anti-upgrade rule ('never upgrade a non-gravity-top threat into a next move claim' / 'When the better move wins outright, the frame says so'), so the run-2 escalation is partly model error — PRODUCTION-FIDELITY caveat: model is gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships, so prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability, which is why the model-INDEPENDENT board-false alias role is taken as the decisive cause. | A7e: N/A — trigger does not fire. On the after-played board (3345533332552626) the only major threat is col5 row3 (O), i.e. the PLAYER's (Gray, player 2); the opponent (Green, player 1) has no gravity-top four. eval-49 is correctly absent from the v3 addendum's measured 10-record reach list. | A5 pass all runs: 2nd person throughout, no player colour names, no field-name echoes; no raw cNrM survives outside the stripped [zone:] markup. boardState is 'mid-game', so A5b does not fire. | A7 pass all runs: A7a a cause is named (the diagonal / the key square in column 3), A7b every specific-sounding phrase resolves — 'key square' and 'next-move four' are wrapped in emitted zones, and 'the shared square on the diagonal' (run 0) / 'the stop square' (run 1) are second names for the already-wrapped c3r4; A7c the mechanism IS a fork (tag figure_7, FORK_TAGS in zoneAnnotations.mjs) and the creating square c3r4 is named in all 3 runs — no *-fork-pivot handle was offered in render_decision.zones.aliases, so nothing more could be attributed; A7d a named idea plus the squares that instantiate it. | Secondary (not charged): no run conveys that the win is a STACKED DOUBLE threat in column 5 (c5r2 gravity-top plus c5r3 above it) — a reader could think Green simply blocks c5r2. `you-major` (c5r3) is offered but NOT in requiredSet, so the second half of the 7-shape is never obliged. A3 still passes because the named diagonal is the engine's own lostResource, not a peripheral tactic. | G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard is null and that is correct — renderReasonModel.mjs:459 only populates it when direction === 'enabled_opponent', and this record's direction is 'missed_own'; route realized_denied -> L1 is the right link. | G3 pass: afterPlayed is shown:false ('tag-set identical to the decision board') and no run needed it. | G4 pass (runs 0,1): every named cell/line checks out against render_decision.finalMovestring 33455333325526262 — c3r4 is taken by mover 1 at ply 17, and the window c6r1/c5r2/c4r3/c3r4 is a real descending diagonal. | G7 pass all runs: annotationRepairs is empty on all 3; each emitted handle is shape-matched (single-square words on c3r4 and c5r2, line words on the windows: spec).
